classPolicy: Public CSS classes are unprefixed; CSS variables and JavaScript hooks use trm.

components.name: accordion
components.accessibility: Use native details/summary with visible labels. Matching, example-specific name values create exclusive groups; omit name for independent panels. Expanded state and keyboard activation are native, not Collapse JavaScript.

components.name: alert
components.accessibility: Choose alert or status according to urgency. Close is cancelable; closed follows element removal. Application code must arrange suitable focus after dismissal; restoration is not automatic.

components.name: avatar
components.accessibility: Give images meaningful alt text and initials a full accessible identity. Name presence indicators independently; do not communicate status only through color. Stacks are presentation, not focus managers; use native links/buttons for actual actions.

components.name: badge
components.accessibility: Static labels and counts need readable context and sufficient contrast. A badge does not supply independent toggle or removal behavior; use native controls for actions.

components.name: bottom-sheet
components.accessibility: A Bottom Sheet is a named native Drawer, not another plugin. Default modal focus and background inertness come from showModal; keep an explicit close button. Data-API opening registers visible-opener focus return. Swipe is only an enhancement, not dragging or snap points.

components.name: breadcrumb
components.accessibility: Name the navigation and ordered hierarchy. Use explicit breadcrumb-link and decorative breadcrumb-divider elements; authored aria-hidden excludes separators. Mark one current item with aria-current=page.

components.name: button
components.accessibility: Use native named controls and explicit action types. Button toggles active and aria-pressed; native checkbox buttons retain checked semantics. Disabled links need an actual activation guard.

components.name: card
components.accessibility: Use meaningful headings and semantic regions, appropriate image alternatives and native action links. Card bodies use flex gaps; joined groups require a query container. No focus or navigation controller is provided.

components.name: carousel
components.accessibility: Name the region, slides and native controls. Initialize before relying on active-slide tracking during direct scrolling. Autoplay needs a visible pause control; focus alone is not an automatic pause policy.

components.name: chip
components.accessibility: Standalone Chip styling supplies no selection, dismissal or keyboard controller. Use native buttons/links for actions, explicitly synchronize aria-pressed and active, name removal targets and arrange focus after removal. The shown application handler is separate from the editable Chips plugin.

components.name: chips
components.accessibility: Label the native ghost input and explain chip keyboard selection. Generated dismiss buttons are named Remove and leave the tab order; authored controls retain their own labels/order. CSS active is not aria-selected, and core supplies no live announcements or submitted value array. These guides disclose explicit focus/contrast CSS and an application-owned JSON submission example.

components.name: collapse
components.accessibility: Use named native buttons, matching aria-controls/targets and initial expanded state. Collapse changes show and aria-expanded, emits cancelable start events and completion notifications; it supplies no accordion arrow-key or automatic focus-restoration policy.

components.name: combobox
components.accessibility: Use a named native button, adjacent Menu, authored listbox/options, labelled search and native disabled options. Options receive real focus; no aria-activedescendant input model or remote fetching is supplied. The generated named hidden input submits one value or a comma-separated string. Combobox notifications do not await Menu completion.

components.name: command-palette
components.accessibility: Optional local extension, not Bootstrap core. It tracks an active descendant and returns focus, but its Tab boundary handler is not native modal inertness or a document-wide focus guard. Give the search a label, keep a close control, and coordinate shortcuts and background focus in your application.

components.name: data-table
components.accessibility: Local optional CSS extension, not a Bootstrap Data Table plugin. Keep captions/scoped headers and labelled native search, sort and checkbox controls. Application code owns data, filtering, order and selection. Plain tables do not gain grid navigation or selection semantics from styling.

components.name: datepicker
components.accessibility: Name the native text input or button and offer a suitable text-entry/native-date alternative. Calendar Pro owns generated grid/button semantics. Typed edits do not automatically resync the adapter selection array; locale display is not an ISO submission guarantee. Keep approved sanitization, same-origin arrow assets and explicit demo contrast styling.

components.name: dialog
components.accessibility: Use a named native dialog and an obvious dismissal control. Modal focus/inertness comes from showModal; modal=false is non-modal. Configure initial focus in markup. Data-API openers register focus return; programmatic callers own their focus policy. Cancelable show/hide differ from completion and hidePrevented notifications.

components.name: divider
components.accessibility: Local optional CSS extension, not a Bootstrap Divider component. Hide purely decorative separators, or name meaningful separator roles and set vertical orientation when appropriate. Separators are not focusable splitters or section headings.

components.name: drawer
components.accessibility: Use a named native dialog with an explicit placement and a button alternative to gestures. Modal state is backdrop || !scroll; only backdrop=false plus scroll=true is non-modal. Root scroll locking depends on scroll. Data-API triggers restore visible opener focus; responsive presentation is CSS, not a custom focus trap.

components.name: empty-state
components.accessibility: Local optional CSS extension, not a Bootstrap Empty State component. Explain the absence with a heading and useful native action. Hide decorative artwork. The explicit demo owns creation, status text and focus; it does not save a project or contact a backend.

components.name: forms
components.accessibility: Use native controls with visible labels, explicit names, instructions and programmatic help/error associations. Checkbox, radio and switch keep native keyboard state. Disabled and readonly differ; feedback and summary focus are application-owned. Forms has no standalone JavaScript plugin.

components.name: list-group
components.accessibility: Choose real list, navigation or control semantics. Native inputs retain selection behavior; CSS active state supplies no controller. Use native disabled or remove/guard unavailable link destinations. Responsive horizontal variants need a query container.

components.name: menu
components.accessibility: Author named native toggles and appropriate content semantics. Menu synchronizes expanded state, supports enabled-item arrows/Home/End and logical submenu keys, and returns focus on Escape. It supplies no typeahead or automatic application-menu roles; unavailable anchors need guarded destinations.

components.name: navbar
components.accessibility: Name the navigation landmark and current destination. Layout expands from the navbar container width, not viewport width. Responsive examples require Drawer JavaScript for native modal focus, Escape and visible-opener focus return. No Navbar plugin or automatic aria-expanded synchronization is supplied.

components.name: nav-overflow
components.accessibility: Keep a named navigation landmark and real destinations. Menu supplies overflow keyboard entry and Escape focus return. Links are cloned and originals hidden; existing menus are relocated. Approved A11Y-001 remaps cloned descendant IDs and local references while preserving originals. Resizing can rebuild an open menu.

components.name: otp-input
components.accessibility: Label the one real text input, retain one-time-code autocomplete, and put errors/help on that input. Generated slots and separators are aria-hidden decoration. Visual masking does not secure or remove the real value. Runtime events use otpInput, not the frozen scanner filename suffix. Test physical RTL tapping and real-device autofill separately.

components.name: pagination
components.accessibility: Name the result navigation, mark one current page and guard disabled destinations. CSS supplies connected link styles, not data fetching or application page state.

components.name: popover
components.accessibility: Default click toggles a non-modal role=tooltip description and does not automatically dismiss on an outside click. A focus trigger supplies outside/focus dismissal. Escape closes without moving focus; no focus trap, roving order or automatic aria-expanded is provided. Prefer concise text and retain sanitization.

components.name: progress
components.accessibility: Name each progress wrapper and keep aria-valuenow/min/max synchronized with its visual value. Stacked segments have their own named progressbar wrappers. Animation does not make a determinate value indeterminate or announce updates automatically.

components.name: range
components.accessibility: Label the native slider and retain native bounds, step and name. Bubble/tick markup is decorative. Use descriptive units or application-owned aria-valuetext when needed; a formatter alone changes only the bubble. The pinned fill and bubble position remain physical left-to-right even in RTL.

components.name: skeleton
components.accessibility: Use real placeholder classes, hide decorative shapes and keep one meaningful loading message outside the busy region. The application replaces content and clears aria-busy. Skeleton is a documentation route alias, not a core CSS class or JavaScript loader.

components.name: spinner
components.accessibility: Give a standalone spinner role=status and hidden loading text, or hide decorative spinners when adjacent status text already explains the operation. Native disabled buttons cannot be activated. Reduced motion slows border/grow; custom rotation has no automatic reduction.

components.name: scrollspy
components.accessibility: Use resolvable fragment links and a named keyboard-focusable scrolling region. Scrollspy changes active classes, not aria-current. Optional smooth navigation settles the hash and focuses the section; ordinary scrolling does not move focus.

components.name: status
components.accessibility: Local optional CSS extension, not a Bootstrap Status component. Visible text carries the state; decorative dots and pulse are supplementary. Create a live region before application updates. CSS does not poll services or announce changes by itself.

components.name: strength
components.accessibility: Pair decorative segments or bar with readable sibling status text and a labelled password input. The plugin does not supply a numeric ARIA meter, authentication policy or breach check. Feedback/events change only when the level changes, not for every different score; the event redacts password text.

components.name: stepper
components.accessibility: Use an ordered list with stepper-item children. Mark completed and current items active, identify one current item with aria-current=step and explain status in text. Stepper provides CSS presentation, not wizard navigation.

components.name: table
components.accessibility: Use captions and scoped headers with explicit status text. Name keyboard-focusable horizontal scroll regions. Stacked data-cell labels are visual generated content, not a replacement for real headers. CSS does not implement sorting, selection or grid keyboard navigation.

components.name: tab
components.accessibility: Author unique trigger/panel IDs, aria-controls, aria-labelledby, initial selection and focusable panels. Tab initializes missing roles and roving tabindex, and supports unmodified arrows/Home/End in DOM order; horizontal arrows are not reversed for RTL.

components.name: timeline
components.accessibility: Local optional CSS extension, not a Bootstrap Timeline component. Preserve chronological list order and valid time values. The actual horizontal scrolling list must be named and keyboard focusable. CSS provides no roving focus or activity-fetching controller.

components.name: toggler
components.accessibility: This JavaScript primitive has no fixed CSS class. Put mutation configuration on each target and use native triggers. It does not synchronize disclosure ARIA, handle Escape, manage focus or implement an outside-dismissal policy. Use Collapse or Dialog/Drawer for those behaviors.

components.name: tooltip
components.accessibility: Use a named focusable trigger and supplemental content. Default hover/focus content is connected with aria-describedby; Escape dismisses without moving focus. Floating UI and template sanitization are required parts of the implementation. Keep essential information visible outside the tip.

components.name: toast
components.accessibility: Create the live region before updates and choose polite status or urgent alert semantics. Initialize and show notifications explicitly; give persistent/actionable messages sufficient time and a named dismissal control. Autohide pauses during hover/focus; no focus move or automatic restoration is supplied.
